shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Post cards at rest on the board. Soft and diffuse — the card lifts off the canvas without competing.

shadows.name: card-dragging
shadows.purpose: Post card being dragged. Doubled shadow signals elevation and active movement.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Floating toolbar, pill navbar, modals, dropdowns. Intentionally deep to separate from the board surface.

shadows.name: signal-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus ring and live-action pulse. Color-based, not elevation-based — communicates state.

shadows.name: signal-glow-soft
shadows.purpose: Ambient glow under accent elements in the hero area and board pulse indicators.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (button hover, input focus).

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Card drag release, modal entry, toolbar reveal. Snappy deceleration.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Button hover, focus ring, icon swaps.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Panel transitions, sidebar collapse, card state changes.

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: Modal entry, sheet open, dropdown reveal.

narrative.overview:
Jackal feels like walking into a studio where a team is actively working. There is warmth in the air, color on the walls, and evidence of decisions in progress. The interface does not present itself as a blank slate waiting to be filled — it is a workspace already inhabited. Tonal warm neutrals and a tactile dot-grid canvas make the board feel physical and grounded. The four brand colors (Frozen Lake, Tangerine Dream, Mint, Ivory) are not decorative accents; they are semantic markers tied to post types, like colored sticky notes pinned to a real corkboard.

Typography is quiet and functional. Geist Sans carries everything without drama. The system earns its character through color and motion, not typographic spectacle. Transitions run at 150–200ms because users in flow notice lag before they notice elegance. The dark sidebar anchors the product with a high-contrast left column that persists even in light mode.

Delight lives in the moments: a confetti burst when a task list hits 100%, pulsing indicators when teammates are present, a smooth card drag that snaps into place. The baseline chrome is restrained; the board surface is where the energy lives.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, tactile neutral surfaces anchored by a persistent dark sidebar
Four semantic brand colors that belong to post types, not to chrome
Single-family sans (Geist) — no typographic decoration, weight does the work
Dot-grid canvas as the board's physical material

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Frozen Lake, Tangerine Dream, Mint, and Ivory are reserved for post-type tinting and board-level state. They do not appear as general decoration on navigation, buttons, or chrome. Their absence from UI structure is precisely what makes them legible as data on the board.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Live Signal Blue is the sole primary action color. It lives on CTAs, focus rings, active selection, and board pulse. Diluting it with decorative uses elsewhere kills its authority.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Geist Sans covers all roles. Do not introduce a second sans or a display typeface. Weight contrast (400/500/600/700) provides hierarchy.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces start flat. Shadows appear only on interactive or elevated elements — cards, modals, floating toolbars. Static structural panels use tonal layering, not shadow.

dos: Do use Live Signal Blue (#0ea5e9) only for primary CTAs, focus rings, active selection, and board pulse.
Do keep the sidebar dark in all modes — it is a deliberate design decision, not a dark-mode artifact.
Do apply the four brand colors to post-type tinting and board-level state only.
Do use the three-step tonal surface stack for structural depth; reserve shadows for interactive elements.
Do run transitions at 150–200ms with ease-out-quart easing.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion alternatives for every animation.
Do maintain 4.5:1 minimum contrast for all body text.
Do use post-card's 18px radius for board content and 10px for UI controls.
donts: Don't use Notion's document-heavy UI patterns: dense nesting, collapsible outline hierarchies, full-page text editor mode as the primary surface.
Don't design generic SaaS landing pages: cream backgrounds, bento grids of identical feature cards, eyebrows on every section, hero-metric number grids.
Don't introduce a second font family. Geist Sans covers all roles.
Don't use the four brand colors (Frozen Lake, Tangerine Dream, Mint, Ivory) as general decoration or hover states on chrome.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text) anywhere.
Don't add decorative motion that doesn't convey state.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px) as accents on cards or list items.
